ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is Br3C—Br, and on the right side is :PPh3; one curved arrow points from the lone pair of electrons on the phosphorus atom to the Br on the right side, and another curved arrow points from the C—Br bond to the carbon atom. Reasoning: this indicates that triphenylphosphine attacks the bromine atom, and the C—Br bond electrons return to carbon, therefore the attacked C—Br bond is broken, generating the tribromomethyl anion CBr3^- and the triphenylphosphine bromonium cation Ph3PBr^+. The corresponding molecular state is represented with SMILES as Br[C-](Br)Br and Br[P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3, and connected with a dot.

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First describe the image: Br3C—Br is shown reacting with triphenylphosphine, :PPh3, with arrows indicating P lone-pair attack on Br and C—Br bond electrons moving onto carbon. Apply the arrow-pushing changes: disconnect C from the attacked Br, attach that Br to PPh3, assign CBr3 a negative charge and PPh3Br a positive charge. Encode the two separated ionic products as SMILES: Br[C-](Br)Br and Br[P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3, joined by a dot.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中左侧是 Br3C—Br，右侧是 :PPh3；一条弧形箭头从磷原子的孤对电子指向右侧的 Br，另一条弧形箭头从 C—Br 键指向碳原子。推理：这表示三苯基膦进攻溴原子，C—Br 键电子回到碳上，因此断开被进攻的 C—Br 键，生成三溴甲基负离子 CBr3^- 和三苯基膦溴鎓正离子 Ph3PBr^+。对应的分子状态用 SMILES 表示为 Br[C-](Br)Br 和 Br[P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3，并用点连接。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as Br3C—Br next to :PPh3. The right curved arrow starts at the phosphorus lone pair and points to the bromine bonded to carbon; the left curved arrow sends the C—Br bond electron pair back toward the carbon side.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use arrow-pushing rules: an arrow tail is the electron source and an arrow head is where the electron pair goes. P donates its lone pair to Br, forming a P—Br bond and making phosphorus positively charged; the C—Br sigma bond electrons move to carbon, breaking the C—Br bond and making CBr3 negatively charged.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing tetrabromomethane-like Br3C—Br and :PPh3. From the arrows, update only the affected bonds: remove the C—Br bond to the leaving bromine and form a P—Br bond. Then check formal charges by normal valences: the carbon fragment with three bromines is [C-](Br)(Br)Br, and the phosphorus fragment with Br plus three phenyl groups is [P+]. Convert these fragments into valid SMILES and separate them with a dot: Br[C-](Br)Br.Br[P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧是一个 Br3C—Br 结构，即中心碳连着三个溴并再与一个溴成键；右侧是带孤对电子的 :PPh3。弯箭头显示 :PPh3 的孤对电子进攻连接在碳上的溴，同时 C—Br 键的电子移向碳。推理：按箭头只改变受影响的键，断开 C—Br 键并形成 P—Br 键。断键后碳片段保留三个 Br，因得到键电子而为三溴甲基负离子 [C-](Br)(Br)Br；磷与三个苯基和 Br 成四键，带正电，为 Br[P+](Ph)3。用 SMILES 表示两个分离片段并用点分隔，得到 Br[C-](Br)Br.Br[P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3。

planner_metadata.image_role: Identify the starting connectivity from the image: a carbon bearing three bromines and bonded to a fourth bromine, plus a neutral triphenylphosphine drawn with a lone pair. Identify the visual electron-flow cues as indicating loss of the C—Br bond and creation of a Br—PPh3 association.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt to determine that the final deliverable is not a mechanism description but the SMILES for the post-relocation molecular state.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use valence and formal-charge accounting. Carbon with three C—Br bonds plus the former C—Br bonding electron pair becomes trivalent carbanion CBr3−. Phosphorus that gains a bond to bromine while retaining three phenyl substituents becomes tetravalent phosphonium, BrPPh3+. The products are separate ionic fragments, so SMILES uses a dot between them.
